definitions.explanation: Stronger and more emotive than {汚|きたな}い — describes something so dirty or unkempt that it looks repellent. The らしい suffix adds a "gives off a ... impression" nuance.

examples.japanese: {汚|きたな}らしい{格好|かっこう}をしている。
examples.english: He's dressed in a filthy, grimy way.

examples.japanese: {床|ゆか}が{汚|きたな}らしくて{座|すわ}れない。
examples.english: The floor is so grimy I can't sit down.

examples.japanese: {汚|きたな}らしい{食|た}べ{方|かた}は{周|まわ}りの{人|ひと}を{不快|ふかい}にさせる。
examples.english: Eating in a disgusting way makes those around you uncomfortable.

notes:
An intensified, more emotional form of {汚|きたな}い (dirty). The らしい here means "looking/seeming," so {汚|きたな}らしい stresses a repellent, unclean impression rather than mere dirtiness.

FORMS:
- Adverbial: {汚|きたな}らしく
- Negative: {汚|きたな}らしくない
- Past: {汚|きたな}らしかった

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {汚|きたな}い: dirty — plainer, less emotive
- むさ{苦|くる}しい: squalid, stuffy — filthy and cramped or shabby

forms.label: Conditional たら
forms.negative: {汚|きたな}らしくなかったら
